name: Lopez
role: U.S. Marine; Larry's friend from the cub scouts
summary: The friend whose invitation Larry credits with his life. On 25 June 1965 Larry was standing in front of the Mỹ Cảnh floating restaurant in Saigon when Lopez — "my pal throughout the cub scouts," by then a Marine — appeared and asked him to eat at the Peacock instead. As they entered the Peacock the Mỹ Cảnh blew up. "It was like a guardian angel… It was a miracle he showed up." Larry says Lopez "just showed up at this moment"; nothing in his account says they had arranged to meet, and nothing says what became of him afterwards. First name not yet given.
researchNotes: Named for the first time on 2026-09-05 (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0068-c18307841.json), in the course of identifying a photograph of the street of flowers. The date of the encounter is fixed by the bombing itself (sources/frus-1964-68-v03-d20); his presence is Larry's testimony alone. A surname-only name, but with two handles most names here lack — a boyhood in the same Inglewood cub scout pack as Larry in the early 1950s, and a Marine posting that put him in Saigon in June 1965 — and both are searchable without asking Larry anything. What to ask him, when the moment comes, is open: 'Tell me about Lopez.' Working notes: research/events/my-canh-bombing-1965.md. Ledger #32, issue #128.
